destination.name: Ballina
destination.tagline: A Richmond River port town whose best-known landmark is a giant prawn.
destination.description: Ballina sits at the mouth of the Richmond River in the Northern Rivers, where settlers formed a settlement in 1842 and the Richmond River Light has been lit since 1880. Its best-known landmark is the Big Prawn, and its urban area runs north to the surf village of Lennox Head. Lennox Point has a long right-hand break, and Seven Mile Beach and Lake Ainsworth fill out the coast. In 1973 the Las Balsas rafts from Ecuador were towed into Ballina, and one is kept at the Ballina Naval & Maritime Museum.
whyVisit: Watch surfers from Pat Morton Lookout

goodToKnow.title: Beginner water at Lake Ainsworth
goodToKnow.detail: The tea-tree-stained dune lake beside Lennox Head has sheltered water that suits beginner windsurfers, while Seven Mile Beach is better known for body surfing and kite surfing.

goodToKnow.title: The prawn is at Bunnings
goodToKnow.detail: The Big Prawn is a giant concrete and fibreglass prawn beside the Bunnings car park entrance, so it is a quick photo stop rather than a half-day outing.

goodToKnow.title: Fly into Ballina Byron Gateway
goodToKnow.detail: The regional airport, about 34 km east of Lismore, serves the Northern Rivers now that Lismore has no passenger flights.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Autumn and spring, {months}, are the milder months for beach walks and surf checks along the Ballina coast.
